subject: Re: SpryTech subscription renewal & path to marketplace billing
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma.park@sprytech.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example; grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@sprytech.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — procurement asks about Marketplace option

Hi Priyom and Grace,

Our annual contract with Redwood is up July 1 and procurement is pushing us to buy through AWS Marketplace to comply with internal purchasing rules. They asked whether we can move to an AWS Marketplace listing and consume via a procurement PO instead of a direct invoice.

Quick context: we’re a public SaaS company (SpryTech) and our finance team needs a Marketplace-friendly contract and an AWS price/SKU mapping to push through the procurement queue. Carlos from procurement is looped in.

Can Redwood provide a runbook for moving from a direct subscription to Marketplace billing (entitlements, SKUs, any proration on renewal, and expected timeline)? Also, any special discounts or listing amendments on renewal that you can apply would help get sign-off faster.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

Best,
Emma
Head of Operations
SpryTech

Attachments: none
From: priyom_das@redwood.example
To: Emma Park <emma.park@sprytech.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.example; karthik_iyer@redwood.example; naomi_feldman@redwood.example
Date: 2028-03-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — procurement asks about Marketplace option

Emma — thanks for the note and for the heads-up. We’ve onboarded several customers to Marketplace mid-contract and can map entitlements so your procurement team sees a clean PO workflow.

High-level we’ll need to: 
- Confirm the current SKU/seat counts and renewal date (I’ll attach a suggested mapping).
- Decide whether you want a full cutover at renewal or a phased entitlements swap (phased often minimizes billing cliffs).
- Confirm whether SpryTech requires any custom pricing/discounting that we must surface on the Marketplace listing (we can do this via an amendment).

I’ve attached a first-pass mapping and a checklist (marketplace_mapping.xlsx, spry_renewal_draft.pdf) — these are drafts to accelerate procurement review. Grace and Karthik — can you weigh in on timeline and whether we should recommend a phased swap? Naomi — please flag any finance controls or SLA implications we should highlight for their procurement team.

If it helps, I can propose a 30-minute call with Carlos next week and include our Marketplace partner manager to walk through DocuSign and PO timing.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: spry_renewal_draft.pdf, marketplace_mapping.xlsx
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example
To: priyom_das@redwood.example; karthik_iyer@redwood.example; naomi_feldman@redwood.example
Date: 2028-03-21T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: SpryTech Marketplace plan (recommend phased swap)

Priyom / team — my recommendation is a phased entitlements repath: keep the current direct seat subscription active and concurrently provision equivalent Marketplace SKUs for new spend and any renewal seats over a short window (30 days). Reasons:

- Minimizes procurement friction (they can submit a PO for immediate items)
- Allows finance to reconcile final counts and avoid prorated refunds/credits at cutover
- Gives CS a safety net if SSO/entitlement sync issues appear

Karthik — can you prepare the exact SKU list and the Marketplace listing lead time? Naomi — run a quick check: will this phased approach impact our revenue recognition or require a credit memo on our side? I’ll draft an email template to send to SpryTech procurement describing steps and timelines.

Grace O’Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example; priyom_das@redwood.example; naomi_feldman@redwood.example
Date: 2028-03-22T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: SpryTech Marketplace plan (SKU list + lead times)

Team — attached is the SKU mapping and an estimate of lead times. Key notes:

- Mapping: prod-sku.redwood.small -> SpryTech core seats; prod-sku.redwood.enterprise -> SpryTech premium seats.
- AWS listing publication typically takes 5–7 business days once the amendment and pricing are signed off.
- For a phased swap we can start provisioning Marketplace SKUs within 48 hours after the PO is issued; final reconciliation and close-out should happen within a 30-day window.
- We’ll need a Marketplace amendment (DocuSign) to record the entitlements shift and any agreed discount.

I’ll attach the spreadsheet (marketplace_mapping.xlsx) to the SpryTech email and include an outlined timeline.

— Karthik
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@sprytech.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example; grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Cc: Emma Park <emma.park@sprytech.com>
Date: 2028-03-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — procurement asks about Marketplace option

Thanks — that all looks good. Procurement prefers the phased approach. They can issue a PO for the first tranche next week pending the SKU list and the DocuSign amendment. Please send the PO-ready SKU table and the DocuSign link so procurement can move forward.

A couple of asks on our side: 
- Please include a single-point contact for billing reconciliation during the 30-day window.
- We’ll need confirmation that moving the entitlements will not change our existing SLA commitments.

If you can get the DocuSign and SKU table to me by EOD Friday (2028-03-25), procurement will start the PO cycle immediately.

Carlos Mendes
Procurement Manager
SpryTech
